title: Kestrel and the Sigil
premise: In the city of Vellamere, magic was outlawed twenty years ago when King Aldric signed the Sigil Accords, sealing the old gods behind a binding carved into the crown itself. Mirabel Montrose, a bone-carver who has quietly heard the dead since childhood, discovers the binding is failing—and the thing that whispered the Accords into existence, a memory-eating entity called the Hollow Regent, is wearing the king and devouring the city's past. When a dead girl's prayer reaches Mirabel through her carvings, she is drawn into an underground network of outlaw hedge-witches, disgraced priests, and one loyal royal guard torn between duty and truth. To free Aldric, Mirabel must carve a counter-sigil from the bones of everyone the Regent has erased—including, at the last, a piece of her own remembered life. In the climax she unbinds the king at the cost of her memories of her lost brother, choosing justice over the comfort of what she loved; the epilogue-tinged final chapters show a city slowly relearning its gods, and Mirabel carving new charms for names she can no longer recall but refuses to let vanish.
about_author: Yara Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funeral records in coastal mill towns before turning to fiction. They write about grief, small magics, and the people history forgets on purpose.

chapters.title: The Bone That Sang
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In her cluttered shop, Mirabel carves a memorial charm for a grieving mother and hears, for the first time in years, not a human voice but something vast and wrong pressing against the edges of the dead's whispers. Emotional beat: unease—the safe, invisible life is cracking.

chapters.title: Prayer of a Drowned Girl
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A river-drowned child's voice begs through a half-finished charm: 'the king ate my name.' Investigating the drowning site, Mirabel finds other bereaved families whose memories of their dead are fraying. Beat: reluctant purpose; she cannot unhear the plea.

chapters.title: The Accords
chapters.summary: Guard Captain Sef Rennick's POV. Rennick, who owes Mirabel a debt from the purges, warns her that the Crown is investigating 'resonant objects.' Flashback to the night magic fell. Beat: loyalty established as both shield and cage.

chapters.title: What the Regent Wears
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At a public audience, Mirabel sees King Aldric up close and senses the hollow thing inside him—patient, hungry, wearing his grief like a coat. She flees before it notices her listening. Beat: dread made personal.

chapters.title: The Lamplighters
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The drowned girl's trail leads to an illegal chapel beneath a tannery, where hedge-witch Odile Ferran keeps a congregation of the half-forgotten. Mirabel learns the Regent eats memory to stay anchored. Beat: finding a fellowship she never wanted.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, interwoven with her brother Tam's remembered voice. A quiet chapter mapping how Mirabel survived the purges by carving silence into herself. Beat: tenderness and guilt; establishes what she stands to lose.

chapters.title: A Guard's Doubt
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Ordered to raid the tannery chapel, Rennick stalls, falsifies a report, and realizes the Regent's ministers are rewriting records wholesale. Beat: the first open crack between law and truth.

chapters.title: Names Eaten
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The congregation holds a rite for a woman no one can remember, and the ritual fails—the Regent has taken even the gods' ability to hold her. Mirabel proposes the forbidden alternative: bone-carving a vessel strong enough to keep a name. Beat: defiant hope.

chapters.title: The Counter-Sigil
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Study of the original binding reveals it was carved from the bones of the gods' last priestess—and that a counter-sigil needs bones freely given by the erased. The mathematics of the working are brutal: many names, or none. Beat: the cost comes into focus.

chapters.title: Ash Wednesday Market
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Crown censors burn 'resonant goods' in the market square; Mirabel's shop is seized and Odile is taken. Rennick, present in uniform, does nothing—and hates himself cleanly. Beat: the net closes; despair.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Odile Ferran
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the White Cells, the Regent speaks through interrogators, offering Odile her erased daughter's name in exchange for the conspirators. Odile lies beautifully and buys three days. Beat: sacrifice sharpened into strategy.

chapters.title: The King's Dream
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV—a mind flickering inside the possession. Brief, disorienting chapter: the real king surfaces while the Regent sleeps, leaving a message scratched into a window: 'I remember my mother's face. Do not let it take that too.' Beat: the enemy is also a victim.

chapters.title: Bone Runners
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Rennick defects in all but name, using guard routes to smuggle Mirabel toward the royal ossuary where the priestess's bones lie. Betrayal by a young runner costs them a day and a life. Beat: loyalty tested under fire.

chapters.title: The Ossuary Beneath
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the ossuary, the dead speak in chorus for the first time in twenty years—the binding thinning. The priestess's ghost teaches Mirabel the sigil's true grammar: it cannot be broken, only answered. Beat: awe; the plan transforms.

chapters.title: What Tam Knew
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A revelation via the chorus: her brother Tam wasn't purged—he gave himself to the first binding willingly, and his name is the keystone the Regent hides deepest. Beat: devastating reframe of her whole life.

chapters.title: Three Days to Coronation
chapters.summary: Braided POVs. The Regent announces a renewal ceremony to re-carve the binding permanently. The cell scrambles: Odile escapes the White Cells with Rennick's help; Mirabel begins carving the counter-sigil's frame. Beat: ticking clock, rising momentum.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The priestess's ghost confirms the keystone requires a name given with love and surrendered with consent—and Tam's consent must come through Mirabel, who must give up every memory of him. Beat: the emotional nadir; grief chosen in advance.

chapters.title: Vigil
chapters.summary: Quiet two-hander, Mirabel and Rennick. On the eve of the ceremony, Mirabel spends her last night remembering her brother aloud while Rennick records nothing, holding witness instead. Beat: stillness before storm; love without possession.

chapters.title: The Renewal
chapters.summary: Climax part one, multiple POVs. At the coronation rite, the Regent begins re-carving the binding as the crowd's memories visibly dim. Mirabel walks into the light, charms singing, and offers the counter-sigil. Beat: terror and resolve.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Mirabel's POV. The Regent offers Mirabel Tam back, whole, if she stops. She names him instead—'Tam Montrose, who chose'—and surrenders the memories mid-word. The counter-sigil answers the binding; the Regent unravels; Aldric wakes weeping. Beat: triumph purchased with self.

chapters.title: After the Unbinding
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Aftermath: Aldric, diminished and mortal, repeals the Accords; the gods return cautiously; Rennick chooses truth-telling over promotion and testifies about the purges. Beat: justice outside the law finally entering the law.

chapters.title: Charms for Forgotten Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, closing. Reopening her shop, Mirabel carves charms for names she no longer remembers, guided by a list in Rennick's handwriting and a feeling like sunlight she can't source. A child asks who Tam was. 'Someone who chose,' she says. Beat: bittersweet peace; memory outliving the rememberer.
